::: {.prose}

Spatially structured populations, like salmon in a watershed, are made up of many interconnected local populations, called a metapopulation. Local processes such as dispersal, productivity, and mortality are often patchy and density-dependent, and they feed back to shape the dynamics of the whole.

For fish and wildlife, management often works at the scale of the whole metapopulation, while stressors tend to act locally. This mismatch between the scale of management and the scale of ecological processes can produce unpredictable patterns.

## Our approach

Together with the Salmon Watersheds Lab, we explore how spatial structure in local density-dependence drives surprising patterns at the metapopulation scale, using:

1. A conceptual model to illustrate the idea
2. A theoretical model to quantify spatial patterns of recovery in linear and dendritic networks
3. A review of empirical case studies across many taxa
